		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Note 7 &#x2013; Restructuring Charges</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:11.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has implemented various initiatives to reduce its overall cost structure, including exiting certain facilities and transitioning work to other locations. Costs incurred in connection with these actions include employee separation costs, including severance, benefits and outplacement, and lease termination, cease use and other related facility exit costs</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">During the fourth quarter 2013, the Company approved and initiated a restructuring plan designed to reduce operating costs, so it can focus its resources on a restructured business model. On January 13, 2014, the Company continued the execution of this plan by notifying the majority of affected employees or commencing consultation processes with affected employees. The complete execution of the restructuring plan will result in a total workforce reduction of approximately 90 full-time positions, or approximately 16% of the Company&#x2019;s combined workforce. The notice periods for employees vary by country. Affected employees are eligible to receive severance payments in exchange for a customary release of claims against the Company in those countries where the severance amounts exceed what is required under applicable law. The Company expects the reduction in its workforce to be completed by the end of the second quarter 2014.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:11.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">For the year ended December 31, 2013, the Company recorded a charge in the amount of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$4.6</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million for</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> employee separation costs and other costs related to employee</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> termination benefits. Such charges were recorded as a component of restructuring charges</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, net</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> in the accompanying consolidated statements of oper</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ations and comprehensive loss</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Substantially, all of these costs are ex</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">pected to be cash expenditures. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">As of December 31, 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$4.2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">million </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">remained accrued and unpaid for these termination benefits, which are reflected as a component of accrued liabilities in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Equity Incentive Plans </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has in effect the 2006 Equity Incentive Plan (&#x201C;2006 Plan&#x201D;) under which it may grant incentive stock options (&#x201C;ISOs&#x201D;), nonqualified stock options (&#x201C;NSOs&#x201D;), and restricted stock units</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (&#x201C;RSUs&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. Through December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company had reserved </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2.3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million shares of common stock for issuance under the 2006 Plan. The shares reserved under the 2006 Plan automatically increases on each January&nbsp;1, beginning in 2006 and continuing through January&nbsp;1, 2016, by the lesser of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">3%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of the total number of shares of common stock outstanding as of December&nbsp;31&nbsp;of the preceding calendar year, or a number of shares determined by the Board of Directors, but not in excess of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">3.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million&nbsp;shares. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Options may be granted for periods of up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ten</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> years and at prices equal to no less than </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">100%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of the fair market value of the underlying common stock on the date of grant. Options granted generally become exercisable over a period of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">four</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> years, based on continued employment, with </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">25%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of the shares underlying such options vesting </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">one</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> year after the vesting commencement date and with the remaining </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">75%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of the shares underlying such options vesting in equal monthly installments during the following three years. Options generally terminate three months following the end of a grantee&#x2019;s continuous service to the Company. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Generally, RSUs vest over two years in equal installments on the anniversary of the vesting commencement date. Upon vesting, the RSUs will convert into an equivalent number of shares of common stock. The amount of the expense related to RSUs is based on the closing market price of the Company&#x2019;s common stock on the date of grant and is amortized on a ratable basis over the requisite service period. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

In addition, leases generally contain provisions for annual rent escalations based on fixed amounts or cost of living increases. The difference between the rent due under the stated periods of the leases compared to rent expense on a straight-line basis is recorded as deferred rent. 			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">On February 20, 2014, the Company entered into a lease agreement for approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">26,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> square feet of office space in Parsippany, New Jersey. The lease will commence on July 1, 2014 and expire on August 31, 2019. 			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Office of the Chief Scientist G</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">rants</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company&#x2019;s research and development efforts in Israel have been partially financed through grants from th</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">at country&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Office of the Chief Scientist</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of the Israeli Ministry of Industry, trade and Labor (&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">OCS</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. In return for the OCS&#x2019;s participation, the</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> Israeli subsidiary is committed to pay royalties to the Israeli Government at the rate of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">3.5%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of sales of products in which the Israeli Government has participated in financing the research and development, up to the amounts granted plus interest.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:11.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Royalties payable to the OCS are recorded as sales are recognized and the associated royalty becomes due and are classified as cost of revenues. For the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">years</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2013 and 2012, royalty expenses relating to OCS grants were </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$0.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$0.8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million, respectively. As of December&nbsp;31, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2013 and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2012, the royalty payable amounted to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$1.2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$1.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, respectively</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. The maximum amount of the contingent liability under these grants potentially due to the Israeli Government (excluding interest) was </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$16.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$16.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million as of December&nbsp;31, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2013 and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2012, respectively.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Indemnification Obligations </font>

		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Agreements between the Company and its customers under which its customers purchase or license products generally have indemnification provisions under which the Company selling or licensing the products is obliged to defend third party claims against the customer arising as a result of the Company&#x2019;s products infringing or misappropriating third party intellectual property rights.&nbsp;Depending on the customer and the nature of the agreement, these claims may or may not have a monetary limitation and generally the Company would not cover indirect, special or punitive damages. These clauses are always contingent on the Company selling or licensing the products being allowed to have full authority to defend or settle the claim with the customer&#x2019;s assistance and </font>

In some agreements, the Company selling or licensing the product to the customer has accepted indemnification obligations related to damages caused by the Company&#x2019;s product or employees which result in death or personal injury or damages as to property.&nbsp;Generally when these provisions are included they are reciprocal and subject to various limitations and carve-outs. 			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company enters into agreements in the ordinary course of business with, among others, customers, systems integrators, resellers, service providers, lessors, sub-contractor, sales representatives, and parties to other transactions with the Company, with respect to certain matters. Most of these agreements require the Company to indemnify the other party against third party claims alleging that its product infringes a patent or copyright. Certain of these agreements require the Company to indemnify the other party against losses arising from: a breach of representations or covenants, claims relating to property damage, personal injury or acts or omissions of the Company, its employees, agents, or representatives. In addition, from time to time the Company has made certain guarantees regarding the performance of its products to its customers. </font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March&nbsp;28, 2011, the Company received a letter from the SEC informing the Company that the SEC was conducting an informal inquiry (&#x201C;SEC Informal Inquiry&#x201D;), and requesting that the Company preserve certain categories of records in connection with the SEC&nbsp;Informal Inquiry. In a follow up discussion with the SEC on March&nbsp;30, 2011, the SEC informed the Company that the inquiry related to allegations of improper revenue recognition and potential violations of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act of 1977, as amended, by former Veraz Networks Inc. business during periods prior to completion of the Company&#x2019;s business combination with Dialogic Corporation. The Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors (the &#x201C;Board&#x201D;), appointed a committee to review these issues, with the aid of counsel, and to make recommendations to the Board as to what, if any, remedial actions would be appropriate.&nbsp;The committee engaged Sheppard Mullin Richter&nbsp;&amp; Hampton LLP (&#x201C;Sheppard Mullin&#x201D;), as outside counsel to the committee. The Board has taken the remedial actions recommended by Sheppard Mullin and the committee and the Company has updated and improved its compliance procedures.&nbsp;In addition, the Company produced documents to the Department of Justice (&#x201C;DOJ&#x201D;), relating to the SEC Informal Inquiry. Sheppard Mullin subsequently became counsel to the Company on this matter. The Company continues to fully cooperate with the SEC and DOJ in connection with the SEC Informal Inquiry. At the current time, the Company cannot determine the probability of or quantify the amount of any fines or penalties associated with the SEC matters discussed above. Based on information currently available to the Company, it believes that any of the allegations, even if true, would not have a material adverse effect on the accompanying consolidated financial statements. </font>

The Company is required to disclose certain information regarding operating segments, products and services, geographic areas of operation and major customers. The Company&#x2019;s chief operating decision maker is the Company&#x2019;s C</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">hief Executive Officer (&#x201C;CEO&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. The Company has one business activity and there are no segment managers who are held accountable for operations, operating results and plans for levels or components below the consolidated unit level. Accordingly, the Company is considered to be in a single </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">reporting segment </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">operating unit </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">structure. 			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company recognizes interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits as a component of income tax expense in the accompanying consolidated statements of operation and comprehensive loss. As of December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012, the reserve for uncertain tax positions included interest and penalties of $0.9 million and $1.1 million, respectively. Interest and penalty expense, net was $0.3 million and $0.5 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012, respectively. As of December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012, the Company classified the liability in the amount of $2.6 million and $2.3 million, respectively, as long term and $0.1 million and $0.3 million, respectively, as short term. The Company anticipates that during the next twelve months the total liability for unrecognized tax benefits may change by $0.1&nbsp;million due to the expiration of different tax statutes or tax settlements. Any reduction due to expiring statutes would impact the Company&#x2019;s effective tax rate. </font>

In addition, the Company may be subject to examination in foreign jurisdictions for the years from 2004 through 2012. </font>

Such unremitted earnings are to be indefinitely reinvested outside the United States. At this time, the Company has deemed it impracticable to determine the amount of any tax payable if these amounts were repatriated. Determination of the liability is largely dependent on circumstances under which the remittance occurs. </font>

		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt 12.2pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">Item&nbsp;</font><a name="Item_9A_Controls"></a><font style="display: inline;">9A. </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Controls and Procedures </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt 12.2pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Disclosure Controls and Procedures </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We maintain disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act) that are designed to provide reasonable assurance that the information required to be disclosed in the reports we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized, and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to management, including our principal executive officer and principal financial officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our management evaluated (with the participation of our principal executive officer and principal financial officer) our disclosure controls and procedures as of December 31, 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">concluded that </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">our </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of December 31, 2013 at the reasonable assurance level.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt 12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"> Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined under Rule 13a-15(f) and Rule 15d-15(f) of the Exchange Act. Our internal control over financial reporting is a process designed under the supervision of our principal executive officer and principal financial officer to provide reasonable assurance regarding the (i)&nbsp;effectiveness and efficiency of operations, (ii)&nbsp;reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of our financial statements for external reporting purposes in accordance with U.S. GAAP, and (iii)&nbsp;compliance with applicable laws and regulations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Management, with the participation of our principal executive officer and principal financial officer, has conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based on the framework set forth in 1992 </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Internal Control</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Integrated Framework</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission as of December 31, 2013.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> Based on this evaluation, management concluded that as of December 31, 2013 our internal controls over financial reporting were effective and the material weaknesses identified in connection with its evaluation of our internal controls as of December 31, 2012 had been remediated. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt 12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Changes in Internal Controls </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">During the period ended December 31, 2013, we </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">substantially </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">completed our remediation efforts related to our controls over revenue recognition and entity level controls. As a result of the completed remediation efforts noted below, there were improvements in internal control over financial reporting during fiscal year 2013 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting (as defined by Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">After the filing of our Form 10-K with the SEC on March 22, 2013, management identified certain accounting misstatements to previously issued financial statements that were the result of material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Exchange Act Rule 12b-2 defines a material weakness as a deficiency or a combination of deficiencies in internal control over financial reporting, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of our annual or interim financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Other than the completed remediation efforts described below, there were no changes to our internal control over financial reporting that occurred in the fourth quarter of 2013 that materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">68</font>

		</p>

			<p style="line-height:100%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:100%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (1)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="line-height:100%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Revenue recognition practices</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">following significant deficiencies existed in internal control over revenue recognition as of December 31, 2012, which aggregated to a material weakness:</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:54pt;"><p style="width:54pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">There was a lack of communication between operations and finance personnel regarding important sales terms.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specifically, non-standard terms were agreed to between operations personnel and a customer that resulted in a misstatement of revenue during the second quarter of 2012.&nbsp; </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:54pt;"><p style="width:54pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">There were ineffective controls over the confirmation of shipments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specifically, a shipment from one of our contract manufacturers occurred on a date that was later than the date originally confirmed. Also, there was a lack of an automated control to ensure that shipping occurs prior to invoicing.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:54pt;"><p style="width:54pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;font-family:Symbol;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">There was a lack of sufficient technical accounting expertise to apply revenue recognition requirements to certain revenue transactions:</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:90pt;"><p style="width:90pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> a)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">finance personnel did not identify that the risk of loss had not passed to the customer for certain revenue transactions occurring at period-ends as a result of using intermediate common carriers that were not customer-designated carriers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under our shipping terms for the majority of our product transactions, risk of loss passes when the customer-designated carrier takes the goods. </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:90pt;"><p style="width:90pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> b)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">finance personnel did not perform an adequate review of key terms and conditions of certain revenue transactions to assess that revenue recognition criteria were met.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">None of the misstatements identified related to this material weakness, either individually or in the aggregate, resulted in a material misstatement to any previously reported financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Remediation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We have implemented the following remediation procedures that have a</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ddressed the material weakness</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> described above. Specifically:</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (a)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Training was implemented with all members of the Sales and Operations Departments so that they better understand the reasons why any change to terms requires communication with and approval of the legal and finance departments; </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (b)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We have discontinued using intermediate common carriers for quarter-end shipments, unless specifically requested by our customers; </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (c)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We have provided additional education and training to members of the finance department regarding revenue recognition rules to enable them to appropriately apply accounting requirements to revenue transactions and perform a sufficient review of terms and conditions of revenue transactions to determine their impact on revenue recognition; and </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (d)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">are working on implementing automated controls which will ensure that invoices are only generated upon actual verified shipment of our product. In the interim, we have implemented manual controls to ensure that invoicing reflects only shipments that were actually processed and that revenue on such shipments is recognized in the correct accounting period. </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt 36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:12pt;"><p style="width:12pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (2)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Breach of entity level controls </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">There was a material weakness identified </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">related to the Control Environment and Information and Communication components of 1992 </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Internal Control</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Integrated Framework</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">This material weakness relates to an inadequate tone within the finance department to implement and maintain an effective control environment in accordance with our Code of Conduct, evidenced by:</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (a)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Communication by the finance department of incomplete information concerning certain financial reporting matters; and </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (b)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Failure of our finance department to communicate and enforce existing accounting policies and procedures.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Remediation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have implemented the following remediation procedures that have addressed the material weaknesses described above. Specifically:</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (a)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We have provided additional education and training on the importance of effective communication within the finance department; </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (b)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:115%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our legal department </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">has </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">provide</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">d</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> training sessions to all employees regarding our enforcement of existing policies and procedures; and </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our legal and human resources departments have implemented a company-wide training program for all employees to enhance knowledge of our existing policies and procedures.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Limitations of Disclosure Controls and Procedures and Internal Control Over Financial Reporting </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our management, including our </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">principal executive officer and principal financial officer</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, do not expect that our disclosure controls and procedures or our internal control over financial reporting will prevent all error and all fraud. A control system, no matter how well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the control system are met. Further, the design of a control system must reflect the fact that there are resource constraints, and the benefits of controls must be considered relative to their costs. Because of the inherent limitations in all control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, within the company have been detected. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Item&nbsp;</font><a name="Item_9B_OtherInfo"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">9B. </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;Other Information </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2014, we entered into a Fourth Amendment (the &#x201C;Fourth Amendment&#x201D;) to the Term Loan Agreement. Pursuant to the Fourth Amendment, the minimum Adjusted EBITDA financial covenant in the Term Loan Agreement is no longer applicable.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2014, we entered into a Twenty-Second Amendment (the &#x201C;Twenty-Second Amendment&#x201D;) to the Revolving Credit Agreement. Pursuant to the Twenty-Second Amendment, the Revolving Credit Agreement was amended to change the minimum Adjusted EBITDA financial covenant and postpone its application until the twelve-month period ending on March 31, 2015. The Twenty-Second Amendment also provides that the EBITDA will not be tested for the periods ending on March 31, 2014, June 30, 2014, September 30, 2014 and December 31, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the Twenty-Second Amendment, the EBITDA</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">remains set at $6.0 million and will be increased by 80% of pro forma adjustment to EBITDA (as set forth in the definition thereof for any applicable Reference Period) concurrently with the closing of each Permitted Acquisition (as defined in the Revolving Credit Agreement).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Revolving Credit Agreement was also amended to increase the &#x201C;Availability Block&#x201D; to $1.4 million, increasing by an additional $100,000 on April 1, 2014 and on the first day of each fiscal quarter thereafter.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:12.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
